outlook.statement: Cane crushing expected to increase to 10 lakh tons for 2026-27 season vs 8 lakh tons previous year due to good rain predictions.

New distillery unit (150 KLPD) to commence full capacity commercial production from 2026-27 season, operating ~250 days, production ~2.55 crore liters; distillery revenue expected to jump by Rs 200 crores.
Power production and vinegar turnover also expected to increase during 2026-27 season due to higher cane crushing.
Global sugar market projected to slip into deficit of 1.7-3.3 million metric tons in 2026/27; Brazil diverting more cane to ethanol; global sugar futures rallying.
India's gross sugar production forecast to recover to ~33.6 million metric tons; domestic prices at record highs; government considering duty-free imports and stricter stockholding limits.
India advancing 20% ethanol blending targets, structurally diverting cane juice and molasses from sugar; integrated mill operating margins projected at 10-10.5%.

no material uncertainty exists as on the date of the audit report that the Company is capable of meeting its liabilities existing at the balance sheet date as and when they fall due within a period of one year from the balance sheet date

risks: Water-intensive crop in drought-prone areas (Maharashtra, Karnataka)
Unpredictable weather and climate change reducing cane yields
Heavy government pricing controls causing farmer payment arrears
Low sugar recovery rates (~9.5-10%) vs global competitors
Aging seed varieties (e.g., Co-0238) with declining pest/disease resistance
Overproduction driving down local sugar prices
Rising expenses for labor, transport, fertilizers squeezing margins
State-mandated high cane prices (SAP/FRP) with controlled sugar sales
Commodity price fluctuations (raw material 60-70% of production cost)
Frequent government interventions, export bans, shifting ethanol-blending rules
Policy unpredictability for investments and long-term revenue
Seasonal crushing (4-7 months) leaving workers/machinery idle
Outdated technology reducing energy efficiency
Competition from local gur/khandsari units for raw cane
Delayed farmer payments straining future supply
Transport delays reducing sucrose content
Environmental strain from water intensity
No element of risk which may threaten the existence of the Company as per Risk Management Committee.
In the opinion of the Committee there is no element of risk which may threaten the existence of the Company.
